one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent never understood that FEN encodes ranks as digit-plus-letter sequences (not coordinate tokens like Ke1/Nf3) and that the fixed sequential re.sub pipeline requires newline-separated replacements to enumerate multiple legal moves, so every re.json it wrote collapsed to a single turn-flip output.
t_err_evidence: cat > /app/re.json writes fundamentally broken regex that flips turn without generating any legal moves
t_commit_evidence: From step 3 onward the agent is locked into a strategy of writing re.json patterns that match coordinate-style FEN substrings and produce single-string substitutions; all subsequent iterations (steps 9, 14, 22, 24, 26, 46, 55, 58, 61, 83, 89, 91, 93) repeat the same fundamental approach without ever correcting the FEN-encoding misunderstanding or adding newline enumeration.
t_surface_evidence: Our moves: 1, Python-chess moves: 20 — FAIL on initial position
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked two critical pieces of knowledge: (1) FEN rank encoding uses digit counts for empty squares and piece letters in sequence (e.g., 'PPPPPPPP', '8', '3B4'), not algebraic coordinate tokens; and (2) the benchmark's fixed run_solution applies re.sub sequentially on a single string and splits on '\n' to get all moves, so re.json must produce newline-delimited outputs to enumerate multiple legal positions. Without understanding either, the agent could only produce a single substitution per FEN input.
